towns.name: Town of Cameron

reporting.basis: Actual results (as reported to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of Local Government Finances)
reporting.scope: All municipal funds, including utilities; schools are run by separate school districts

sources.label: U.S. Census Bureau, 2022 Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances, individual unit file
SC State Ethics Commission, contributions to Town of Cameron's local candidates since 2023
OpenStreetMap license-plate cameras (as mapped by DeFlock and other contributors)
EFF Atlas of Surveillance (police surveillance technology, searched by department)

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2022, as the municipality reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2022 is the latest available.
Public schools are run by separate school districts, and Calhoun County provides many other services; residents pay the town, the county and the school district.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.

Political money counts contributions from businesses, unions and PACs to candidates for town council and mayor, filed with the State Ethics Commission since 2023. South Carolina allows business contributions. Individuals and party and candidate committees are not counted.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Cameras: 4 license-plate cameras are mapped inside Town of Cameron's borders in OpenStreetMap (4 made by Flock Safety), not counting cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies. Flock cameras count as a red flag whoever runs them. Other brands count only when the government is the recorded operator, since many have no operator recorded.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for South Carolina yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Flock camera network
redFlags.detail: 4 Flock Safety license-plate cameras are mapped inside Town of Cameron's borders in OpenStreetMap. Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is not recorded; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.
